title: Late Breaking Results: Improving Deep SNNs with Gradient Clipping and Noise Exploitation in Neuromorphic Devices
problem: Deep SNNs trained with soft resets are computationally expensive and unsuitable for neuromorphic hardware; hard reset-based SNNs suffer performance degradation without gradient clipping.
motivation: Neuromorphic devices fundamentally use hard resets; bridging the gap between training algorithms and hardware constraints is essential for practical neuromorphic computing.
method: Proposes gradient clipping technique for hard reset-based SNN training; explores exploitation of device noise to enhance learning performance; evaluates across multiple datasets and models.
key_novelty: Device noise can be leveraged to enhance SNN learning performance in hard reset regime, contrary to treating noise as pure interference.
contributions: Gradient clipping technique improving training performance in hard reset SNNs
Demonstration that device noise enhances rather than degrades learning
Bridges algorithmic-hardware gap for practical neuromorphic computing
limitations: Full hardware validation on neuromorphic devices not discussed.
primary_theme: Noise-aware SNN training for neuromorphic hardware
